The characters' dynamics in the provided text highlight the central tension between illusion and reality, which drives the overarching themes of the novel. Jay Gatsby’s relentless pursuit of Daisy Buchanan is not merely a romantic endeavor but a symbolic attempt to reclaim an idealized past and achieve the American Dream. This dynamic underscores the theme of the corruption of the American Dream, as Gatsby’s belief in its attainability clashes with the "insurmountable societal barriers" and the "hollowness" of materialistic values. Daisy, as the object of this idealization, represents the unattainable reality that Gatsby constructs in his mind. Their interaction reveals the futility of trying to force reality to conform to illusion, ultimately leading to Gatsby’s tragic downfall. This dynamic serves to critique the era's values, showing how the pursuit of such dreams, when detached from reality, leads to destruction rather than fulfillment.

The primary use of a bed is for sleeping.
